question.text: A volatility smile in options markets indicates that:

answer.text: Options with strikes far from ATM have higher implied volatilities than ATM options
ATM options always have the highest implied volatility
Implied volatility is constant across all strike prices
Only call options show varying implied volatilities

explanation.text: The Logic: A volatility smile is the pattern observed in option markets where implied volatility, when plotted against strike price for a single expiry, is higher for strikes that are deep in-the-money and deep out-of-the-money than for at-the-money strikes — forming a U-shape. It reflects market pricing of tail risk that the constant-volatility assumption of basic option-pricing models does not capture. The Trap: If IV were constant across strikes, the plot would be flat — no smile. ATM does not have the highest IV in a smile. The smile applies to both calls and puts at the same strike (by put-call parity their implied vols match). Note: The NISM-Series-IV Interest Rates Derivatives workbook (Dec 2025) pages 133-144 cover option types, moneyness, premium factors, and implied volatility, but do not specifically describe the volatility smile/skew. The framing above is general derivatives-market knowledge.
